findings.slide_ref: Week 10 - Database Views and Authorization_.pdf page 9
findings.claim: Strong password policies prevent unauthorized user access: ... Implement password expiration and lockout mechanisms
findings.citation_excerpt: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT require subscribers to change passwords periodically.
findings.suggested_replacement: Drop the periodic password-expiration recommendation. Per NIST SP 800-63B (current revision -4, August 2025), verifiers SHALL force a password change only if there is evidence the authenticator has been compromised. Pair long passwords (≥15 chars), screening against breach corpus blocklists, salted+hashed storage with a memory-hard KDF, rate-limiting on failed attempts, and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., WebAuthn/FIDO2) instead of forced rotation.

findings.slide_ref: Week 10 - Database Views and Authorization_.pdf page 9
findings.claim: Use complex passwords and multi-factor authentication (MFA).
findings.citation_excerpt: Other composition requirements for passwords SHALL NOT be imposed.
findings.suggested_replacement: Drop 'complex passwords' guidance based on character-class composition rules (mixed case, digits, symbols). Per NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.1, composition rules SHALL NOT be imposed; instead require a 15-character minimum (8 with MFA), allow up to 64+ characters including spaces and Unicode, screen prospective passwords against a blocklist of breached/common passwords, and keep the MFA recommendation.
